what_happened: Live machine state showed sapience-app's guard config.json had already been hand-patched (coalesce_s=300, net_timeout_s=15) matching the dispatch's starting proposal, but deadline_s (8.0) was left unraised and sf1-engine's config was untouched -- discovered by reading live state directly rather than relying solely on the dispatch's carried figures, which surfaced a new deadline_s < net_timeout_s bug not in the dispatch text.

Verified from guard.py source (not assumed) that detaching a checkout also silently stops commit-event reporting (main_postcommit/main_postrewrite gate on mode=='attached' via _session()), which directly confirms the dispatch's claim about CONSENT-benjamin.json's hub_commit_events dependency and grounds the stay-attached recommendation.

Dispatch description's '35 failures (24 TimeoutError, 11 URLError)' and '~2% per-call failure rate' conflate 3 distinct initiating suspension events with 35 downstream 'stopped earlier' blocks produced by the sticky marker. Re-derived live: 38 blocks total, of which only 3 are initiating (2 TimeoutError 2026-11-13 13:35 and 2026-11-17 09:46, 1 URLError 2026-11-17 11:49). Per-round-trip failure rate is ~0.17% (3/1720), not ~2%; expected-survival-~50-actions figure is correspondingly wrong, though the observed stall outcome is unchanged.

Found a SECOND fail-closed no-retry surface neither the dispatch nor the research report covers: guard.py send()'s sender breaker (breaker.json). It is OPEN in BOTH attached repos -- sapience-app since 2026-11-15 17:16, sf1-engine since 2026-11-14 23:04 -- with 85 and 106 commit events stranded in outbox/ (191 total). Code prints 'breaker open, no retry' explicitly. This means the hub_commit_events reporting consented in CONSENT-benjamin.json has been silently dead for 2-3 days, which is material to the detach question (goal 4), the upstream defect write-up (goal 3), and the visibility surface (goal 5). Plan extended to cover it.
